source_caption:
The Usual Suspects is a crime thriller directed by Bryan Singer that follows a group of criminals brought together for a mysterious job after a police lineup. The story is mainly told through the interrogation of Verbal Kint, played by Kevin Spacey, who describes how the group got involved in a dangerous plan linked to a legendary crime lord named Keyser Söze.

As Verbal narrates the events, the film constantly shifts between past and present, keeping viewers guessing about what’s real and what’s not. The movie builds tension through clever storytelling and an unpredictable plot, leading to one of the most famous twist endings in film history. It explores themes of deception, identity, and manipulation, leaving the audience questioning everything they just watched.

source_details.synopsis: The Usual Suspects is a 1995 crime thriller film directed by Bryan Singer and written by Christopher McQuarrie. It stars Kevin Spacey, Gabriel Byrne, Benicio del Toro, Stephen Baldwin, Kevin Pollak, Chazz Palminteri and Pete Postlethwaite. The plot follows the interrogation of Roger "Verbal" Kint, a small-time con man, who is one of only two survivors of a massacre and fire on a ship docked at the Port of Los Angeles. Through flashback and narration, Kint tells an interrogator a convoluted story of events that led him and his criminal companions to the boat, and of a mysterious crime lord—known as Keyser Söze—who controlled them.
